canonical_statement: The prespecified renal analysis evaluated the long-term renal effects of empagliflozin within EMPA-REG OUTCOME.
EMPA-REG OUTCOME was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled cardiovascular outcomes trial; this report focuses on prespecified renal microvascular outcomes.
Participants had type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease.
Eligible participants had baseline eGFR of at least 30 mL/min/1.73 m² by the MDRD formula.
Participants assigned to empagliflozin received 10 mg once daily in addition to standard care.
Participants assigned to empagliflozin received 25 mg once daily in addition to standard care.
The comparator was placebo once daily in addition to standard care.

exposures.details: Matching placebo added to standard care.

canonical_statement: Renal safety assessments included acute renal failure using the narrow standardized MedDRA query, including the preferred term acute kidney injury, and hyperkalemia using two MedDRA preferred terms.
Baseline eGFR was assessed with the MDRD formula, whereas prespecified longitudinal renal-function assessments used the CKD-EPI creatinine equation.
Analyses used a modified intention-to-treat approach among patients who received at least one dose of study drug.
Microvascular analyses used nominal alpha 0.05 without correction for multiple hypothesis testing.
No formal a priori power calculations were performed for microvascular outcomes.
Time-to-event renal outcomes were compared using Cox proportional-hazards models adjusted for study group, age, sex, baseline body-mass index, baseline glycated hemoglobin, baseline eGFR, and region.
Prespecified comparisons included pooled empagliflozin doses and each individual dose versus placebo.
Longitudinal eGFR changes were assessed with mixed-model repeated-measures analyses and random-intercept/time-coefficient models for prespecified slope periods.
Incident or worsening nephropathy was defined as progression to macroalbuminuria, doubling of serum creatinine with eGFR ≤45 mL/min/1.73 m², initiation of renal-replacement therapy, or renal death.

outcome.definition: Progression to macroalbuminuria; doubling of serum creatinine accompanied by eGFR ≤45 mL/min/1.73 m²; initiation of renal-replacement therapy; or death from renal disease.

canonical_statement: A total of 7020 patients at 590 sites in 42 countries received at least one dose of study drug.
More than 99% of treated participants had established cardiovascular disease.
At baseline, 17.8% of patients had eGFR 45–59 mL/min/1.73 m².
At baseline, 7.7% of patients had eGFR 30–44 mL/min/1.73 m².
At baseline, 28.7% of patients had microalbuminuria.
At baseline, 11.0% of patients had macroalbuminuria.
At baseline, 80.7% of patients were receiving an ACE inhibitor or angiotensin-receptor blocker.
Median treatment duration was 2.6 years and median observation time was 3.1 years.

canonical_statement: The supplementary appendix presents prespecified subgroup analyses for incident or worsening nephropathy and separate analyses by empagliflozin dose.
The treatment effect on incident or worsening nephropathy was directionally consistent across the prespecified subgroups shown in Figure S1.
Supplementary Kaplan–Meier analyses separated empagliflozin 10 mg, empagliflozin 25 mg, and placebo for incident or worsening nephropathy.
The supplementary appendix includes post hoc renal analyses in patients with prevalent kidney disease and in patients with baseline macroalbuminuria.

Longitudinal eGFR plots in Figure S7 stratified patients by baseline eGFR <60 versus ≥60 mL/min/1.73 m² and showed the characteristic early dip followed by slower chronic decline with empagliflozin in both strata.

Supplementary Tables S1–S8 provide renal-stratified baseline characteristics, cardiovascular medication use, microvascular outcomes, sensitivity analyses, prevalent-kidney-disease outcomes, adverse events, complicated urinary-tract-infection terms, and laboratory changes.

Protocol Revision 4 (15 October 2013) explicitly defined new-onset albuminuria, new-onset macroalbuminuria, the composite microvascular outcome, and new or worsening nephropathy before publication of the renal results.

Protocol Revision 4 defined new or worsening nephropathy as new macroalbuminuria, doubling of serum creatinine with MDRD eGFR ≤45 mL/min/1.73 m², initiation of continuous renal-replacement therapy, or renal death.

outcome.definition: Progression to macroalbuminuria; doubling of serum creatinine accompanied by eGFR ≤45 mL/min/1.73 m²; initiation of renal-replacement therapy; or death from renal disease.

canonical_statement: The Publication Statistical Analysis Plan states that its additional analyses were planned in addition to the clinical-trial protocol and trial SAP and were not in contradiction to the trial SAP.

The Publication SAP prespecified additional microvascular endpoints including sustained eGFR reductions, sustained albuminuria transitions, ESRD-related composites, and multiple CKD-EPI eGFR slope intervals.
The Publication SAP specified an on-treatment analysis of secondary microvascular/renal endpoints using events through the minimum of treatment stop plus 30 days or the end of individual observation.

The Publication SAP specified Kaplan–Meier displays and Cox proportional-hazards models for microvascular time-to-event endpoints, with incidence-only presentation allowed when event counts were too small for Cox modeling.
The Publication SAP specified descriptive statistics and mixed-model repeated-measures analyses for continuous renal endpoints and subgroup analyses for new or worsening nephropathy.

The authors concluded that, in patients with type 2 diabetes at high cardiovascular risk, empagliflozin added to standard care was associated with slower progression of kidney disease and lower risk of clinically relevant renal events than placebo.
The authors interpreted the initial eGFR decrease and post-discontinuation rebound as consistent with reversible glomerular hemodynamic changes.
Empagliflozin did not prevent incident albuminuria in patients with normal albumin excretion at baseline.
The renal/microvascular analyses were not supported by formal a priori power calculations and used nominal alpha without multiplicity correction.
The study population was selected for established cardiovascular disease/high cardiovascular risk, limiting direct generalizability to lower-risk type 2 diabetes populations.
The small number of Black participants limited conclusions about renal effects in Black patients.
The hard renal composite of doubling serum creatinine, renal-replacement therapy, or renal death was a post hoc analysis rather than a prespecified primary renal endpoint.
